items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: In that call he gave me a fairly stiff price what his estimate, what it would cost, and we did, as it were, a preview.

ctx.x: Sy Rosen. This same man, Sy Rosen. He now had gone from the Pittsburgh Symphony to the Philadelphia Orchestra where he was manager, to now running Carnegie Hall. And isn’t that something? In that call he gave me a fairly stiff price what his estimate, what it would cost, and we did, as it were, a preview. We did one single concert. It began to rain at three o’clock in the afternoon, and it rained I think until four o’clock the next morning. It was like the South Pacific. But we didn’t have an empty seat. And we…
I don’t mean to keep bringing up Manny again, but he talked about that too, about trying to write for strings and make them swing, and he basically said don’t bother.
